source: Climate Resilient Broadcasting Rice Growing Technique (ASPIRE/IFAD, MAFF, 2018); CARDI Rice Pest brochure (FAO-funded, Plant Protection Program)
text:
Rice blast (ជំងឺឪតឡាត): diamond-shaped lesions with a gray center and brown margin on leaves; under heavy nitrogen use and drought stress it can kill young seedlings (leaf blast) or rot the panicle neck at heading (neck blast), cutting grain fill sharply. Reduce risk by avoiding excess nitrogen especially early in tillering, choosing a variety with known blast tolerance, and treating seed in hot water at about 53-54°C for 10 minutes before sowing; reach for fungicide only once an outbreak is already confirmed and severe.

Bacterial leaf blight (ជំងឺរលាស): yellow-white lesions with a wavy edge running along the leaf margin and veins, spread by wind-driven rain and by irrigation water, and often worse after storm damage tears leaf tissue open. Reduce risk with adequate plant spacing for airflow, avoiding excess fertilizer, and using certified disease-free seed.

False smut / sheath issues at heading: infection around the booting stage can leave grains shriveled or discolored inside the husk; this is associated with excess nitrogen combined with high humidity at flowering. Brown spot and narrow brown spot show up as oval or narrow brown lesions on leaf and sheath and are frequently linked to nutrient deficiency (particularly potassium) or poor seed storage quality rather than a new infection alone.

Before treating any of these, confirm the actual cause: drought stress, waterlogging, nutrient deficiency, and herbicide injury can all produce symptoms that look like disease. Never name a specific fungicide product or rate without checking it against current Cambodian registration for that crop and pathogen.
